children: Global bond yields are paring their early morning gains, with the 10-year Treasury yield hovering around 5% after jumping past that threshold earlier in the day.

The 10-year yield rose as high as 5.040%, its highest level since 2007, before falling back. The retreat matched moves in oil prices, with Brent crude futures trading around $105 a barrel, after climbing past $108 earlier in the day.

The closure of a crucial crude pipeline in Saudi Arabia has rattled investors this week, sending energy prices higher and stoking fears that even tighter oil supplies could add to inflationary pressures.

Together, the moves have dialed up the pressure on the Federal Reserve ahead of Wednesday's interest-rate decision. Investors now see a 93% chance that officials increase rates by a quarter-percentage point, according to CME Group data, up from 59% a week ago.
U.S. stocks opened lower, with the Dow industrials leading modest declines. Indexes in Europe were mixed and closed in the red in Asia.
